hook: There's a color you can't see.

scenes.line: Your eyes have three color receptors: red, green, blue.
scenes.visual_prompt: A human eye in cross-section, three distinct cone cells glowing red, green, and blue against a dark anatomical background, clean and scientific.

scenes.line: A mantis shrimp? Sixteen different color receptors firing at once.
scenes.visual_prompt: A mantis shrimp in vibrant shallow coral reef water, its segmented eyes rotating, surrounded by a kaleidoscopic aura of impossible iridescent hues and wavelengths.

scenes.line: It sees ultraviolet, infrared, polarized light—colors without names.
scenes.visual_prompt: A split-screen: on the left, a coral reef in normal human colors; on the right, the same reef glowing with impossible neon purples, yellows, and shimmering wavelengths our brain can't render.

scenes.line: To that shrimp, your world is basically black and white.
scenes.visual_prompt: A mantis shrimp hunting in slow motion through blurred, desaturated prey—the mantis's view sharp and hyper-saturated, the prey's camouflage invisible to human eyes but blazing neon to the shrimp.

cta: If you could add one new sense humans don't have, would you pick mantis shrimp vision or something completely different?
